guide.title: Soft-Tissue Injuries & Wound Care
guide.lead: Most wounds look worse than they are, but a few hide real danger. Stabilise impaled objects, save amputated parts properly, cover evisceration, and watch any crushed limb for compartment syndrome.

sections.title: Special wounds
rows: Remove (unless it blocks the airway, is through the cheek blocking care, or prevents CPR)
Moist saline gauze → sealed bag → on ice or in ice water
Put it directly on ice or submerge it
Moist sterile dressing plus an occlusive layer; keep warm
Keep the flap attached, gently replace, moist dressing

groups.title: Compartment syndrome
items: Pain out of proportion and on passive stretch (earliest)
Then paresthesia, pallor, paralysis, cold, pulselessness (late)
Loosen dressings and splints; limb at heart level; urgent surgery

groups.title: Crush syndrome (long entrapment)
items: On release: high potassium, myoglobin, arrhythmia, kidney injury
IV fluid before release where possible; cardiac monitor; ALS

sections.title: Tetanus (CDC)
items: Clean minor wound: booster if more than 10 years since the last dose
Other wounds: booster if more than 5 years
Unknown or fewer than 3 doses, dirty wound: vaccine plus tetanus immune globulin
Note the risk and the vaccination history in your handover

quiz.q: A 3 cm jagged glass wound exposing muscle is:
Crush injury: pain out of proportion and pain on passive finger stretch. Suspect:
options: Compartment syndrome: loosen dressings, transport for fasciotomy
Moist saline gauze, sealed bag, on ice or in ice water
Dry gauze in a bag on ice
quiz.explanation: Direct ice causes frostbite; soaking macerates.

options: Stabilise it with bulky dressings; don't remove
Cut it flush to the skin
quiz.explanation: It may be plugging a bleeding vessel.

options: Moist sterile dressing plus an occlusive layer

quiz.q: When may an impaled object be removed?
options: It blocks the airway or prevents CPR
quiz.explanation: Or through the cheek preventing airway or bleeding control.

quiz.q: After 4 hours trapped under rubble, the danger on release is:
quiz.explanation: IV fluid before release where possible; monitor.

quiz.q: Tetanus booster for a dirty wound if the last dose was more than:
A degloving flap attached by a pedicle:
options: Keep it attached, gently replace, moist dressing
Pain out of proportion and on passive stretch

flashcards.question: Laceration vs incision vs avulsion
flashcards.answer: Laceration: jagged tear. Incision: clean cut. Avulsion: tissue torn away (flap or complete).

flashcards.question: Evisceration
flashcards.answer: Don't replace organs; moist sterile dressing plus an occlusive layer; keep warm; transport.

flashcards.question: Amputated part
flashcards.answer: Moist saline gauze → sealed bag → on ice or in ice water. Never directly on ice. Label and transport with the patient.

flashcards.question: Removing an impaled object
flashcards.answer: Only if it blocks the airway, is through the cheek and blocks airway or bleeding control, or prevents CPR. Otherwise stabilise.

flashcards.question: Compartment syndrome signs
flashcards.answer: Pain out of proportion and on passive stretch (earliest), paresthesia, pallor, paralysis, poikilothermia, pulselessness (late).

flashcards.question: Tetanus
flashcards.answer: Toxin causes muscle spasm (lockjaw). High-risk wounds: puncture, dirty, crushed, dead tissue, delayed care.

flashcards.question: Tetanus booster timing
flashcards.answer: Clean minor: more than 10 years. Other wounds: more than 5 years. Unknown or under 3 doses: vaccine plus immune globulin for dirty wounds.

flashcards.question: Crush syndrome
flashcards.answer: After long entrapment, release floods potassium and myoglobin: arrhythmia and kidney injury. IV fluid before release, monitor, ALS.

critical.scenario: Rebar through the left lower abdomen, still set in a concrete block. BP 98/64, HR 118, pale and sweaty.
critical.question: Best approach?

options.t: Stabilise the rebar with bulky dressings, have rescue cut the debris without moving the bar, transport to a trauma centre
Pull it out to lighten the load
options.f: It may be plugging bleeding vessels.

options.t: Rock it gently to free it
Wait for it to be removed on scene by fire crews

critical.kpi: Stabilises an impaled object and coordinates extrication

critical.scenario: A man with diabetes caught his foot in a farm auger 2 hours ago: wound full of soil. He can't recall his last tetanus shot.
critical.question: Approach to tetanus?

options.t: Clean and dress the wound, document it as high-risk and the unknown vaccination status, and hand over the need for vaccine plus immune globulin
Only if he's had no shot in 20 years
options.f: Dirty wound: more than 5 years or unknown.
Irrigate with clean water or saline.

critical.explanation: Contaminated, crushed and delayed: all high-risk.
critical.kpi: Recognizes a tetanus-prone wound and documents risk

critical.scenario: A motorcyclist has a large lower-leg degloving: an 8 × 10 cm flap hanging by a pedicle, active bleeding, exposed muscle. BP 88/60, HR 130.
critical.question: Management?

options.t: Control bleeding with pressure (tourniquet if it's life-threatening), gently replace the flap, moist dressing, treat for shock, trauma centre
Clean it thoroughly on scene first

critical.explanation: A tourniquet is for bleeding pressure can't control.
critical.kpi: Manages an avulsion while prioritizing shock
